ground: Dean Court (sponsored name: the Vitality Stadium)
memory: 2025-26: finished sixth, the best in the club's history, to reach Europe for the first time

lingo.means: The club nickname. Most people put it down to the cherry-red striped shirts. Another story credits the cherry orchards that once stood by the ground.
The ground's proper name, after the Cooper-Dean family, who gave the club the land in 1910. The sponsor calls it the Vitality Stadium, but plenty of fans still say Dean Court.
The club began as Boscombe FC in 1899, and the ground sits on the edge of Boscombe. Some older fans still call the club Boscombe.
Short for AFC Bournemouth. Used in chat, on social media and on the club's own channels.
The 2008-09 season. The club started on minus 17 points after administration and still stayed in the Football League. Steve Fletcher scored the late winner against Grimsby in the last home game.
The north stand, named after the club's record appearance maker. It's where the noisiest home fans gather, and part of it became safe standing in 2024.

lines.t: Up the Cherries!
lines.m: All-purpose rallying cry, before or after a game.

lines.t: Small ground, big noise.
lines.m: Fans are proud that the smallest ground in the league can be one of the loudest.

lines.t: We started a season on minus seventeen and still stayed up.
lines.m: The Great Escape of 2008-09. Fans bring it up when anyone calls them a small club.

lines.t: It's Dean Court to me, whatever the sign says.
lines.m: The old name still wins with long-time fans.

lines.t: Bournemouth in Europe. Never thought I'd see the day.
lines.m: The club's first ever European campaign came after the sixth-place finish in 2026.

lines.t: Seen worse. We were nearly out of the league once.
lines.m: A long-time fan's way of shrugging off a bad result.

lines.t: Saints can say it isn't a derby. We know it is.
lines.m: Southampton fans tend to say Portsmouth is their real derby. Bournemouth fans see it differently.

traditions.name: Red and black stripes
traditions.means: When the club became AFC Bournemouth in 1971 it switched to red and black stripes modelled on AC Milan's. The stripes are still the home kit fans think of as proper.

sore.why: They won on the final day at Everton and still went down because Villa drew. It still stings.

pronounce.why: Locals end it with a short 'muth'. Outsiders say 'Bourne-mouth', and it's noticed straight away.
The b is silent and the end is a short 'kum', not 'comb'.

avoid.why: Saying 'mouth' at the end marks you as a visitor.
The club's name puts the AFC first.

avoid.say: the South Coast derby against Saints
avoid.why: The South Coast derby means Southampton against Portsmouth.

unsure: ground: the Vitality naming deal ran to summer 2026; Vitality's 2026-27 shirt deal was described as a stadium-and-shirt partnership, but I found no formal naming renewal, so Dean Court leads

memory: The Invincibles: unbeaten through the 2003-04 league season

lingo.means: An Arsenal fan. The word grew out of 'the Gunners' in the 1980s, and fans use it with pride.
The old-fashioned way of naming the club, still heard in 'Up the Arsenal'. Saying it marks you as a proper fan.
Short for 'Come On You Gunners'. Written in posts and shouted at games.
The day it becomes certain Arsenal will finish above Spurs. A fan site came up with it in 2002.
The 2003-04 side that went the whole league season unbeaten.
Arsenal's old ground, left in 2006. Older fans still talk about it fondly.
The stand named after the clock that hung at Highbury. The clock moved to the Emirates and the name came with it. The North Bank is the end opposite.

lines.t: Up the Arsenal!
lines.m: Classic rallying cry. Note the 'the'.

lines.t: Come on you Gunners!
lines.m: Everyday cry before kick-off, often written COYG.

lines.t: Twenty-two years we waited. Champions again.
lines.m: Arsenal won the 2025-26 league, their first title since the Invincibles.

lines.t: I still miss Highbury, but the Emirates is home now.
lines.m: A typical older fan's view of the 2006 move.

lines.t: One-nil to the Arsenal. Job done.
lines.m: After a narrow win. It borrows the old terrace favourite from the George Graham years.

lines.t: Nothing beats a North London derby win.
lines.m: Beating Spurs matters more than almost anything.

lines.t: Happy St Totteringham's Day!
lines.m: The greeting once Arsenal are sure to finish above Spurs.

traditions.name: North London Forever
traditions.means: Louis Dunford's 'The Angel (North London Forever)' is played before home games, and the whole ground joins in.

traditions.name: Yellow ribbons
traditions.means: Fans wear yellow ribbons to cup finals, a nod to the yellow away kit and the old terrace favourite 'She Wore a Yellow Ribbon'.

sore.why: Lost to Barcelona in 2006 and to PSG on penalties in Budapest in 2026. The big one is still missing.

avoid.why: Fans never add the FC when talking.

avoid.say: Arsenal haven't won the league since the Invincibles
avoid.why: Arsenal won the 2025-26 title. The old jibe is out of date.
Praising the big rival is a dead giveaway.

memory: 1982: beat Bayern 1-0 in Rotterdam to win the European Cup, with a Peter Withe goal

lingo.means: Short for 'Up The Villa'. Fans sign off messages and posts with it.
The big home stand behind one goal, where the loudest fans go.
Nickname for the team and its fans. Spelt with one i.
Another club nickname, from the lion on the badge.
The club's traditional motto. It was dropped from the badge in 2016 to make room for a bigger lion.
Villa against Birmingham City, played since 1879. Birmingham calls itself Britain's second city.

lines.t: Up the Villa!
lines.m: The classic rallying cry, often written UTV.

lines.t: See you in the Holte.
lines.m: Arranging to meet in the home end at Villa Park.

lines.t: Rotterdam, '82. Best night in our history.
lines.m: Recalls the 1982 European Cup win.

lines.t: We founded the Football League, you know.
lines.m: Villa director William McGregor set up the league in 1888. Fans like to point it out.

lines.t: Thirty years without a trophy, then Istanbul. Worth every minute.

lines.t: Blues? Never mind them.
lines.m: Mild dismissal of Birmingham City, the big local rival.

traditions.name: The Bells Are Ringing
traditions.means: A long-standing fans' favourite that became the official club anthem in 2011, after a push by supporters.

traditions.name: Flags in the Holte
traditions.means: The 1897 Group, a supporters' group, organises the big flag and tifo displays at Villa Park.

sore.why: It ended 29 straight years in the top flight. Fans would rather not relive that season.

pronounce.why: Rhymes with 'bolt'. The final e is silent.

avoid.why: Nobody shortens the club to 'Aston'. It's always Villa.

avoid.say: Villa and Birmingham, same thing really

avoid.say: Villa haven't won anything in years
avoid.why: The trophy drought ended in Istanbul.

ground: the Gtech (Gtech Community Stadium, home since 2020)
memory: 2021: beat Swansea 2-0 in the Championship play-off final to reach the top flight for the first time in 74 years

lingo.means: The club nickname. In the 1890s, students from Borough Road College shouted 'buck up Bs' for a friend in the team, and the local papers wrote it down as Bees.
The old ground, 1904-2020, famous for a pub on every corner: the Griffin, the Princess Royal, the New Inn and the Brook.
Fans' nickname for the small two-tier Brook Road stand at Griffin Park.
Fans' short name for the current stadium by Kew Bridge, opened in 2020 as the Brentford Community Stadium.
The supporters' trust that ran the club in the 2000s, before selling to Matthew Benham in 2012. It still has a seat on the board.

lines.t: Come on you Bees!
lines.m: Everyday rallying cry.

lines.t: I miss a pint on all four corners.
lines.m: Nostalgia for Griffin Park and its four pubs.

lines.t: Seventy-four years we waited to get back up there.
lines.m: Brentford last played top-flight football in 1947, until promotion in 2021.

lines.t: Nine play-offs we lost before that day at Wembley. Nine!
lines.m: Brentford failed in nine play-off campaigns, a national record, before winning in 2021.

lines.t: Get Hey Jude going!
lines.m: What fans say when they want the crowd joining in after a win.

lines.t: Beating QPR still means the most.
lines.m: QPR are the old West London enemy. In 1967 they tried to take over Brentford and move into Griffin Park.

traditions.name: Hey Jude
traditions.means: The Beatles' 'Hey Jude' is Brentford's terrace anthem, belted out before and after games.

sore.why: Nine failed play-off campaigns before 2021, including four lost finals. Fans laugh about it now, but outsiders shouldn't.
A stoppage-time penalty on the last day would have won promotion. It hit the bar and Doncaster scored at the other end.

avoid.why: They left Griffin Park in 2020.
Brentford is in west London, and its rivals are QPR and Fulham.
Being new to the Premier League doesn't make the club new.

memory: 2011: the Amex opened at Falmer, ending 14 years without a proper home ground after the Goldstone was sold in 1997

lingo.means: What fans usually call the club, as in 'Up the Albion'.

The American Express Stadium at Falmer, home since 2011.
The old ground in Hove, home for 95 years until the board sold it in 1997.
The council athletics track the club used from 1999 to 2011. Fans who stuck with it wear it as a badge of honour.
The home end at the Amex, where the loudest fans sit.

lines.t: Up the Albion!
lines.m: Classic rallying cry.

lines.t: Never take the Amex for granted.
lines.m: A nod to the homeless years at Gillingham and Withdean.

lines.t: We played home games in Gillingham, seventy miles away.
lines.m: The two-year groundshare after the Goldstone was sold. Fans who went never forget it.

lines.t: Europe again. Not bad for a club that nearly went under.

lines.t: Palace week. Nothing else matters.
lines.m: How fans feel before the Palace game.

lines.t: Five-nil against Palace. Never getting tired of that.
lines.m: Brighton beat Palace 5-0 in October 2026, their biggest win in the fixture in seven decades.

traditions.name: Sussex by the Sea
traditions.means: The 1907 county song plays as the teams come out. Since 2014 the music cuts out before the end and the crowd finishes the chorus on its own, then applauds.

sore.why: Gordon Smith's late chance against United in extra time was saved, and Brighton lost the replay 4-0.
The old ground was sold in 1997 and the club saw little of the money. Older fans are still angry.

avoid.why: Crystal Palace are the big rival.
The Goldstone was sold in 1997. The Amex has been home since 2011.
It's a media name. Fans of both clubs don't use it.

memory: 2012: won the Champions League for the first time, beating Bayern on penalties in their own stadium

lingo.means: Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's home since 1905.
The south stand. From the 1960s it was the home of the loudest fans, and the name still carries that history.
The club nickname, from the royal blue shirts.
Fond short name for the club, as in 'Up the Chels!'

lingo.ipa: ˌkeɪ tiː biː ɛf ɛf ˈeɪtʃ
lingo.means: A fans' sign-off, short for a phrase about keeping the blue flag flying high.

lines.t: Up the Chels!
lines.m: Everyday rallying cry.

lines.t: See you down the Bridge.
lines.m: Arranging to meet at the ground.

lines.t: 2012, Drogba's penalty. Best night of my life.
lines.m: Recalls the first Champions League win.

lines.t: We've won all four of the big European trophies. Name another club that has.
lines.m: The 2025 Conference League win made Chelsea the first club to win all four main UEFA competitions.

lines.t: Blue Is the Colour at the Bridge. Still gets me.
lines.m: The 1972 club anthem is still played on matchdays.

lines.t: Club World Cup winners. World champions, mate.
lines.m: A favourite boast since the 3-0 win over PSG in the 2025 final.

lines.t: Beating Spurs never gets old.
lines.m: Tottenham are the London rival fans most enjoy beating.

traditions.name: Blue Is the Colour
traditions.means: The club anthem, released before the 1972 League Cup final. It reached number five in the charts and is still played at the Bridge.

traditions.name: Carefree
traditions.means: The fans' best-known terrace song, set to the tune of a hymn.

sore.why: The 2026 FA Cup final defeat to Man City made it seven domestic cup finals lost in a row.
The Champions League final was lost to United on penalties after the captain slipped taking his kick.

avoid.why: It's a rival fans' dig, not something supporters say.
That nickname went out with the old Chelsea Pensioner crest in the 1950s.

avoid.say: Chelsea had no history before the money
avoid.why: The first league title came half a century before the big spending. Fans hate the jibe.

ground: the CBS Arena (Coventry Building Society Arena, formerly the Ricoh Arena)
memory: 1987: beat Tottenham 3-2 after extra time at Wembley to win the FA Cup, the club's only major trophy

lingo.means: Short for Coventry, the city and the club. Said with a short o, as in 'cot'.
What the club's support calls itself.
Jimmy Hill's shake-up as manager in the early 1960s: new sky blue kit, new nickname, new club song.
The old ground, left in 2005. Older fans still talk about it.
Northampton's ground, where Coventry had to play home games in 2013-14 during a rent row. Most fans stayed away in protest.
The spot where protesting fans gathered during the Sixfields season, named after Jimmy Hill.

lines.t: Come on you Sky Blues!
lines.m: Everyday rallying cry.

lines.t: Twenty-five years we waited to get back up.
lines.m: Coventry returned to the Premier League in 2026, after going down in 2001.

lines.t: Houchen's header, 1987. Best goal ever.
lines.m: Recalls the diving header in the FA Cup final win over Spurs.

lines.t: It's our ground now. Took long enough.
lines.m: The club bought the stadium in 2025, after years of rows over rent and ownership.

lines.t: Champions with ninety-five points. Some side, that.
lines.m: Coventry won the 2025-26 Championship by a distance.

lines.t: We followed them to Northampton. This is nothing.
lines.m: A long-time fan's way of shrugging off a bad day, recalling the Sixfields exile.

lines.t: Leicester's the one I want.
lines.m: Leicester City, up the M69, are the rival fans most want to beat.

traditions.name: The Sky Blue Song
traditions.means: Club anthem written in 1962 by Jimmy Hill and director John Camkin to the tune of the Eton Boating Song. It was first played at a home game that December, and fans still belt it out.

sore.why: The hedge-fund owners' rows led to relegations and a season playing home games in Northampton. Fans fought them for years.
Lost to Luton on penalties at Wembley, a step from the Premier League.

pronounce.why: Locals use the short o of 'Cov'. Many outsiders, and most Americans, say 'KUV-en-tree'.

avoid.why: Locals say it with a short o, as in Cov.

avoid.say: The Sky Blues? You mean Man City?
avoid.instead: In Cov, the Sky Blues means Coventry
avoid.why: Coventry have been the Sky Blues since the 1960s.

memory: 2025: beat Manchester City 1-0 at Wembley to win the FA Cup, the club's first major trophy

lingo.means: The club nickname since 1973, brought in by manager Malcolm Allison.
The old nickname, from the glass Crystal Palace building the club is named after.
How older fans name the club, as in 'Up the Palace!'
The Holmesdale Road stand, home of the loudest fans.
Short for Selhurst Park, home since 1924.

lines.t: Up the Palace!
lines.m: Classic rallying cry.

lines.t: South London and proud.
lines.m: Fans' motto about where the club comes from.

lines.t: Wembley 2025. I cried like a baby.
lines.m: Recalls the FA Cup final win over Man City.

lines.t: FA Cup, Community Shield, then a European trophy. What a year.
lines.m: Palace won the 2025 FA Cup and Community Shield, then the 2026 Conference League in Leipzig.

lines.t: Nothing like Selhurst under the lights.
lines.m: Pride in the old ground's atmosphere.

lines.t: Brighton week. Can't sleep.
lines.m: How fans feel before the Brighton game.

traditions.name: Glad All Over
traditions.means: The Dave Clark Five's 1964 hit has been played at home games since that year. The whole ground joins in.

traditions.name: The eagle flight
traditions.means: Before home games a live eagle flies across Selhurst Park: Kayla from 2010 to 2020, and Phoenix since 2024.

Ahead against Man United, then beaten after extra time.

avoid.say: Palace play at the Crystal Palace stadium
avoid.why: The athletics stadium in Crystal Palace Park is a different place.
Brighton are the biggest rival.
It's a media name. Fans of both clubs don't use it.

memory: 1984-85: league champions and European Cup Winners' Cup winners in the same season

lingo.means: An Everton fan. The word supporters use for themselves.
Semi-official nickname, coined in 2002, that fans use with pride.
Old nickname for Everton's passing football, from a 1920s remark that the team played 'scientific' football.
Fond name for Goodison Park, the men's home from 1892 to 2025.
'Come On You Blues', a common sign-off among Evertonians.
The dock on the Mersey where the new stadium stands, and what many fans call the ground.

lines.t: Come on you Blues!
lines.m: Everyday rallying cry, often written COYB.

lines.t: Nil satis nisi optimum.
lines.m: The club motto: 'nothing but the best is good enough'. Often quoted with a wry smile.

lines.t: We were at Anfield first, you know.
lines.m: Everton played at Anfield until 1892, when a row with the landlord led to the move and to Liverpool's founding.

lines.t: More seasons in the top flight than anyone.
lines.m: Everton have missed only four top-flight seasons since the league began in 1888.

lines.t: Z-Cars comes on and the hairs stand up.
lines.m: The walk-out music still gives fans goosebumps.

lines.t: Goodison will always be special, but Bramley-Moore is home now.
lines.m: A typical fan's view of the 2025 move.

lines.t: We're due a trophy. It's been since 1995.

lines.t: Win the derby and the city's blue for a week.
lines.m: Bragging rights over Liverpool count for a lot.

traditions.name: Z-Cars
traditions.means: The players walk out to the Z-Cars theme, based on the Liverpool folk song Johnny Todd. Everton have done it since the early 1960s, and fans revolted the one time it was swapped out, in 1994.

traditions.name: The Toffee Lady
traditions.means: Before kick-off a teenage girl in old-style dress walks round the pitch throwing Everton Mints into the crowd, a nod to the toffee shops the nickname came from.

sore.why: Nothing major since the 1995 FA Cup. Fans can joke about it; outsiders shouldn't.
Everton were docked points twice in 2023-24 for breaking spending rules, including a record 10-point penalty, later cut to six.

pronounce.why: Goodison's famous home end is spelt the Welsh way but said like 'Gladys'.

avoid.why: The men's team moved in 2025. Goodison now hosts Everton Women.

avoid.instead: Everton are the city's older club

avoid.instead: Founder members of the Football League

lingo.means: Craven Cottage, home since 1896, and the little pavilion in its corner that gives the ground its name.
The club nickname. Fans also call the team the Whites.
Johnny Haynes, Fulham's greatest player, also called Mr Fulham. The Stevenage Road stand now carries his name.
The home end, and the noisiest part of the ground.
The stand along the Thames, rebuilt and finished in 2025.
The 2002 Intertoto Cup, Fulham's only European trophy. Fans joke about it in a self-mocking terrace song.
The fans' campaign while the club played at QPR's Loftus Road in 2002-04 and the Cottage's future was in doubt.

lines.t: Come on you Whites!
lines.m: Classic rallying cry. Fulham play in white.

lines.t: Best walk to any ground in London.
lines.m: Fans love strolling along the river through Bishop's Park to the Cottage.

lines.t: Juventus, 4-1. I was there.
lines.m: Recalls the 2010 Europa League comeback.

lines.t: We're London's oldest professional club.
lines.m: Fulham were founded in 1879, and fans like to remind people.

lines.t: Never the loudest, but the best ground in London.
lines.m: Fans know the Cottage can be quiet. They don't mind.

traditions.name: The walk through Bishop's Park

traditions.name: Palladio

pronounce.why: The h is silent. Outsiders often say 'Full-ham'.

avoid.why: Stamford Bridge is Chelsea's ground, even though it's in Fulham.

lingo.means: The club nickname, from the black and amber stripes.

The old ground, home for 56 years until the move in 2002.
The stadium's name from 2002 to 2016. Plenty of fans still call it that.
Hull against Grimsby or Scunthorpe, the clubs across the Humber estuary.

lines.t: Up the Tigers!

lines.t: Hull City. Not Hull Tigers.

lines.t: Amber and black, through and through.

Bragging title claimed by whichever of Ipswich or Norwich is doing better.
